Not sure what you're up to - it sounds overly complicated to me. For a backup, all you need to do is to copy the Thunderbird profile to a place of your choice while Thunderbird is closed. https://support.mozilla.org/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data#w_backing-up-a-profile

Restoring the backup is trivial, copy the backed up profile back to the actual profile location.

For IMAP accounts, make sure to turn on 'synchronization' for all folders, so that there is actually something you can back up. Synchronization means that Thunderbird downloads an offline copy of all your messages to the local disk. https://support.mozilla.org/kb/imap-synchronization

There is no point backing up the application itself.

H-S Feldman said
Received messages show as tabs - rather than listings and are often repeated ..

I am not sure what is your grievance. Received messages are not automatically shown as tabs, they are displayed in the thread pane in "Table" or in "Cards" view. Your picture shows that you open messages by a double-click to read them in tabs. And much worse: if you use View > Sort By > Threaded and you double-click on a collapsed thread, all single messages of the conversation will be opened in new tabs!

Thunderbird has a built-in feature to automatically restore the previous session upon the next start. So, if you don't close all those message tabs before closing Thunderbird, all of them will be displayed again when launching Thunderbird the next time.

If you want to avoid all those message tabs you may open messages by simple click to read them in the "message pane" instead: To display the message pane hit the F8 key.

content: First, i cannot fix this. I am writing to share a possible problem. There is a file in the POP account named, popstate.dat. This little file saves the identifier for the last downloaded mail. BUT, if the file is corrupted, or if it is prevented from being updated, possibly by intervention by antivirus or VPN or other software, the last downloaded message does not get updated. Because of that, thunderbird keeps downloading from the beginning. I suggest you look at the file in windows file explorer to see the last date it was updated. that may be a clue for you.
